entries.proposition: The series is seven patients from five consanguineous families with homozygous ELOVL1 variants; only one patient's plasma and fibroblasts were studied biochemically.
entries.snippet: Seven cases from five unrelated families were included in the study, four of whom were female.

entries.proposition: The shared neurological picture is a movement disorder with head tremor, myoclonus, dystonia, axial hypotonia and dysarthria; counts exclude cases with unknown status.
entries.snippet: Additionally, all cases exhibited a movement disorder characterized by axial hypotonia (6/6), head tremor (7/7), dystonia (4/7), myoclonus (6/7), and dysarthria (6/6).

entries.proposition: MRI shows hypomyelination in 6 of 6 imaged, a thin corpus callosum in 5 of 6, and no progression on repeat imaging in one patient.
entries.snippet: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain revealed hypomyelinating leukodystrophy (6/6), also affecting the cerebellum and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum (5/6) (Fig. 1B). Hypomyelination was independent of age at imaging and repeated magnetic resonance imaging in case 1 showed no progression.

entries.proposition: The summary comparison table lists seizures as absent for recessive ELOVL1 disease and present for recessive ELOVL4 disease.
entries.snippet: Spasticity + + + − − − Seizures − − + − − − Movement disorder + − − − − −

entries.proposition: Plasma VLCFA was measured in one patient only.
entries.snippet: Analysis of VLCFAs in plasma was performed only in case 1 and demonstrated a decrease in C24:0 and C26:0 concentrations, consistent with the function of ELOVL1 in the synthesis of C22‐C26 VLCFAs (Supplementary Table S2).

entries.proposition: Supplementary Table 2 compares the patient with four siblings: C24:0 18 versus 26.5-32.7 nmol/mL and C26:0 0.21 versus 0.34-0.68 (the comparison group is four siblings of the patient; the sibling-4 C22:0 cell reads 0.41 where the other four values are 30.9-47.4).
entries.anchor: Supplementary Table 2, C24:0 and C26:0 rows

entries.proposition: Supplementary Table 2: the C22:0 row, whose last cell (0.41) does not match the ratio printed for the same sibling (C24:0/C22:0 0.65 implies C22:0 near 45).
Only the nonsense variant in case 1 reaches likely-pathogenic by ACMG; the four missense variants are VUS.
entries.snippet: According to American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines the ELOVL1 variant c.462G>A would be classified as pathogenic (PVS1_VS, PM2_P, PM3_P), the c.248C>T variant as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS)

entries.proposition: The variant tested biochemically is the nonsense variant c.462G>A (p.Trp154*) in case 1 only.
entries.snippet: c.462G>A (p.Trp154*) in case 1; c.248C>T (p.Ser83Leu) in cases 2 and 3; c.457 T>C (p.Trp153Arg) in case 4; c.491G>A (p.Gly164Asp) in case 5; and c.52C>T (p.Arg18Trp) in cases 6 and 7

entries.proposition: The antibody used to show absence of ELOVL1 protein in patient fibroblasts is raised to residues 250-277, C-terminal to the truncation at residue 154, so it cannot detect a truncated product.
entries.snippet: As expected for a nonsense variant, Western blot analysis using a polyclonal antibody targeting the C‐terminal peptide sequence of ELOVL1 (amino acids 250–277, C‐ELOVL1) detected no signal in whole cell extracts from case 1 fibroblasts (Fig. 3A).

entries.proposition: A truncated FLAG-tagged W154X protein is expressed in transfected HeLa cells and localises to the ER, yet shows reduced elongation activity.
entries.snippet: However, an in vitro elongation assay conducted on ELOVL1‐W154X demonstrated a substantial reduction in enzymatic activity compared to ELOVL1‐WT (Fig. 3F).

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 3F-G. 3F: relative elongation of C22:0-CoA by W154X about 0.57 of wild type (about 1.0), n = 3, two asterisks; expression level of the construct is not normalised in the panel. 3G: patient-fibroblast mRNA relative to one control line: ELOVL1 about 0.15, ELOVL2 about 2.3, ELOVL3 about 0.65, ELOVL4 about 0.45, ELOVL5 not significant, ELOVL6 about 1.35, ELOVL7 not detectable.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 3F bar chart 'Relative fold change' ELOVL1-WT about 1.0 and ELOVL1-W154X about 0.57 with two asterisks; Fig 3G grouped bars for ELOVL1 to ELOVL7, control black and patient dotted, with asterisks.

entries.proposition: Other ELOVL transcripts shift in the patient's fibroblasts; this is one patient line against one control, and the paper says only speculation can distinguish compensation from dysregulation.
entries.snippet: Analysis of mRNA levels for other known ELOVL enzymes showed a significant decrease in ELOVL3 and ELOVL4 expression, along with a notable increase in ELOVL2 and ELOVL6 mRNA expression, indicating widespread dysregulation of VLCFA metabolism because of the variant (Fig. 3G).

entries.proposition: Plasma metabolomics: all sphingomyelins are lower in the patient.
entries.snippet: Specifically, all sphingomyelins (SMs) exhibited a substantial decrease in the plasma of case 1 (Fig. 4B).

entries.proposition: Fibroblast lipidomics: C24:0 ceramide and C24:0 hexosylceramide fall, shorter-chain species rise.
entries.snippet: We found reduced levels of VLCFA C24:0‐ceramides and C24:0‐HexCer, coupled with an increase in shorter chain lengths of Cer and HexCer (Fig. 4C,D).

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 4A and 4F-H. 4A: heat map with three patient columns against four control columns (one patient; the three columns are not described as separate individuals). 4F-G: C24:0/C22:0 ceramide ratio about 1.65 in control against about 0.42 in the patient, and for hexosylceramide about 2.35 against about 0.45. 4H: sphingomyelin C24:0/C22:0 about 0.85 against about 0.5; C26:0/C22:0 near zero in both.

entries.proposition: The authors state the genotype-phenotype correlation cannot be established and that genetic modifiers and dietary VLCFA intake may contribute.
entries.snippet: The sample size was too small to establish a definitive genotype–phenotype correlation.

entries.proposition: The proposed link between ELOVL1 and ELOVL4 deficiency is a plausibility argument.
entries.snippet: It, therefore, seems plausible that ELOVL1 deficiency might also cause functional ELOVL4 deficiency because of the lack of C26‐VLCFAs as a substrate for the elongation reaction thereby explaining the overlap of symptoms.

entries.proposition: The truncated-protein mechanism is stated as speculative.
entries.snippet: However, this remains speculative, as no direct structural or interaction data were obtained.
